articles.rephrased_article: The White House announced a plan to impose tariffs on 60 economies, citing concerns about forced labor in goods trade. Greer stated that the US expects the European Union to fulfill its obligations under the Turnberry agreement.

articles.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit: Rajeev Thakkar of PPFAS MF explains when to hold, when to exit, and why most investors get it wrong - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Thakkar, CIO and Director at PPFAS Asset Management, emphasized the importance of long-term investing, stating that investors should avoid selling stocks based on short-term fluctuations or news flow. He cautioned against "profit booking" and highlighted the detrimental effects of frequent buying and selling on compounding returns.  Thakkar stressed the need for patience with strong businesses and diversification to mitigate risk. Investors should acknowledge mistakes early and exit positions when necessary, such as due to structural disruption or excessive valuations. Thakkar also recommended a phased approach to selling, gradually reducing exposure rather than making large transactions. He emphasized that successful investing is about avoiding unnecessary activity and maintaining long-term portfolios for compounding returns.

articles.title: New bill by Chip Roy targeting H-1Bs seeks to end lottery, OPT: Put America's white-collar workers first - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rep. The bill, which would also end Optional Practical Training (OPT), comes amidst ongoing investigations into alleged fraud within the OPT program, with authorities identifying thousands of students potentially linked to suspicious employers.

articles.title: Mumbai in top 50 global cities vulnerable to heat risk | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: University of Oxford researchers have identified 14 Indian cities as among the most vulnerable to heat risk due to El Niño conditions. The study, which analyzed living conditions in 205 global cities, found Mumbai, Nagpur, and Pune ranked highly on a vulnerability index that considers factors like hazard exposure, coping capacity, and socio-economic vulnerability.  The report emphasizes the importance of comprehensive heat risk planning beyond simply focusing on temperature extremes, suggesting strategies that address both hazard exposure and vulnerability to ensure equitable access to thermal comfort for all.

articles.title: Shilpa Shinde on Sanjay Kohli’s reaction to sexual harassment confession: ‘He thanked me’ | Television News - The Indian Express

She claimed she filed the complaint out of desperation and felt trapped, but later retracted it after reaching a settlement with Kohli.  Shilpa Shinde has faced backlash from celebrities like Hina Khan who condemned her actions. Gurleen Baruah, an organizational psychologist and executive coach, explained that productivity is not solely determined by working hours but also by individual working styles and focus. She emphasized that both cultures have valuable lessons to offer, highlighting the importance of cultural exchange for diverse teams.

articles.title: DK Shivakumar Keeps Finance, Priyank Kharge Is Karnataka's New Home Minister
articles.rephrased_article: DK Shivakumar has retained the finance, cabinet affairs, intelligence, and personnel and administrative reforms portfolios in Karnataka. G Parameshwara, the deputy chief minister, will oversee the revenue and sports departments.  Priyank Kharge, son of Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, was given the home department (excluding intelligence) along with IT, biotechnology, and e-Governance responsibilities. Other key portfolios were distributed among 13 other MLAs who took oath as ministers yesterday following Siddaramaiah's resignation.

articles.title: Putin Calls India Reliable Partner, Slams "Detrimental" Western Interference
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin stated that India is a reliable partner and the two nations will continue to deepen their economic and diplomatic relations. He praised India's economic growth, stating it is one of the world's leading economies with impressive rates of growth.  Putin expressed confidence that bilateral trade between the two countries will reach $100 billion soon. Putin also asserted that Western attempts to pressure India into scaling back its cooperation with Russia are futile and damaging to global stability.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow soars 800 points to hit record as Iran optimism offsets chip slump, weak jobs data - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged to a record closing high, boosted by gains in healthcare and financial stocks.  However, the Nasdaq Composite ended essentially unchanged, with chipmaker Broadcom missing revenue expectations, sending its shares tumbling. The U.S. House of Representatives passed a measure blocking President Trump from continuing the war on Iran, while a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon offered optimism for a near-term resolution to the conflict.  Despite these positive developments, initial jobless claims unexpectedly rose, and first-quarter labor costs and productivity were revised lower.

articles.title: Delhi University Professor Living Alone Found Murdered In Her Locked Flat
articles.rephrased_article: Devosmita Paul, an Assistant Professor at Shivaji College, was found dead in her locked flat in Vasundhara Enclave, East Delhi. Her sister, Devarati Paul, discovered the body after breaking down the door. Preliminary investigations indicate that she suffered head injuries and severed veins in her wrist, suggesting a homicide. The police have filed a murder case and are investigating the incident.

articles.title: Ready For "Full Ceasefire": Volodymyr Zelensky In Open Letter To Vladimir Putin
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelensky proposed a face-to-face meeting with Vladimir Putin in a letter, urging the Russian leader to end the war through direct engagement. The Ukrainian president stated his willingness to hold a ceasefire for negotiations and called for a clear date for such a meeting.  The Kremlin confirmed that the letter had not yet been shown to Putin, but offered him an open invitation to meet in Moscow at any time.

articles.title: Rahul ‘selling panic’, promoting baseless conspiracy theories: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Rahul Gandhi of promoting fear and baseless conspiracy theories about the Indian economy and institutions.  Amit Malviya, BJP IT Cell head, countered that Mr. Gandhi's claims about an "economic tsunami" and a collapsing system were unfounded. He highlighted India's resilience in the face of global challenges, citing strong reserves, low inflation, and robust economic indicators.

articles.title: Hundreds protest in Libya outside UN agency against undocumented migrants | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of Libyans protested outside the UNHCR headquarters in Tripoli, accusing the agency of settling undocumented migrants in the country. The protesters demanded the closure of the UNHCR headquarters and accused the agency of seeking to settle undocumented migrants in Libya.  The UNHCR affirmed the rights of all Libyans to express their opinions but warned against spreading misinformation about its work.

articles.title: Russia kills 12 in Ukraine as Kyiv mourns 707 children killed since 2022 | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched attacks across Ukraine, killing at least 12 people and injuring dozens more. The strikes occurred as Ukraine commemorated the deaths of over 707 children killed by Russia since the start of the war in February 2022. Attacks targeted multiple regions including Donetsk, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk, with significant damage to civilian infrastructure.  President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for a face-to-face meeting between himself and Vladimir Putin to end the conflict. The Kremlin responded by offering an invitation for Zelenskyy to meet in Moscow at any time.

articles.title: Brandy Melville: Why is this teen fashion retailer closing its fitting rooms?
articles.rephrased_article: Brandy Melville, the one-size fashion retailer, is closing all fitting rooms in its US stores. This move has sparked outrage among young shoppers who are frustrated by the lack of try-on options and feel alienated by the brand's decision.  Employees at several locations have confirmed that they were instructed to dismantle the changing rooms without explanation, citing vandalism as a reason for the change. The company has not issued an official statement about the decision.

articles.title: 'Happens In Families': Benjamin Netanyahu Plays Down Donald Trump's "F***ing Crazy" Remark
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister, downplayed reports of a serious rift with Donald Trump, US President, stating that disagreements are occasional and usually centered on strategy.  Trump acknowledged using strong language during a phone call about Israel's military operations in Lebanon, but later sought to soften the episode, emphasizing his commitment to working with Netanyahu. Despite the reported disagreement, both leaders remain aligned on preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. They maintain frequent contact and view each other as "great friends."  The two leaders are united in their concern for Iran's nuclear ambitions and have collaborated on efforts to pressure Tehran.

articles.title: Liverpool appoint Spaniard Iraola as new manager in place of Slot | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Liverpool has appointed Andoni Iraola as their new manager, replacing Arne Slot.  Iraola left his role at Bournemouth and is expected to implement a more aggressive style of play, similar to the one that characterized the team under former manager Jurgen Klopp. He earned praise for his tactical acumen and development of young players during his time with Bournemouth, where he led them to a sixth-place finish in the Premier League. Iraola's appointment comes after Liverpool struggled under Slot, who failed to maintain their position at the top of English football.

articles.title: UFC Freedom 250: Donald Trump says Eiffel Tower-like UFC structure may stay at White House - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has compared the UFC structure being built at the White House to the Eiffel Tower, stating he may keep it permanently.  The event, called UFC Freedom 250, will take place on June 14th and is expected to draw a large crowd of military personnel and members of the public. The UFC has invested $60 million in the project, which includes a unification bout between Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje.  The White House has hosted recreational sports events in the past but this marks the first professional live sporting event on its grounds.

articles.title: Block the bombs: Support grows for US bill to restrict arms for Israel | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Block the Bombs Act, which seeks to restrict arms transfers from the United States to Israel, has gained significant support in Congress.  While it initially garnered only 21 Democratic co-sponsors, the bill now boasts 73, representing a "historic" shift in public opinion. Advocates argue that this progress reflects growing awareness of Israeli atrocities and a desire for US investment in domestic needs over military aid. However, despite the increased support, the bill has yet to be brought to a vote on the House floor due to Republican opposition.  Congresswoman Delia Ramirez, who introduced the legislation, emphasizes the need for action and calls for a shift in Congressional priorities away from unconditional support of Israel.

articles.title: Rahul ‘selling panic’, promoting baseless conspiracy theories: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Rahul Gandhi of promoting fear and baseless conspiracy theories about India's institutions and economy.  Amit Malviya, the BJP's IT Cell head, countered that Mr. Gandhi's claims were unfounded and that the Indian economy was resilient despite global challenges. He cited strong reserves, low inflation, robust infrastructure spending, and record FDI inflows as evidence of India's economic strength.

articles.title: Marjane Satrapi: Oscar-nominated Persepolis author and director dies aged 56
articles.rephrased_article: Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian author and illustrator known for her graphic novel series "Persepolis", has died at age 56.  The Élysée Palace called her a leading figure in French culture, whose work carried a universal message and earned her international renown. The artist's death was attributed to sadness following the loss of her husband, Mattias Ripa. President Emmanuel Macron praised Satrapi as a great artist who transformed an Iranian childhood into a universal fable.  Her graphic novel, "Persepolis", depicted her life during and after the Iranian Revolution and earned critical acclaim for its powerful portrayal of Iranian culture and the struggle against oppressive regimes.

articles.title: Zeynab Javadli: Ex-wife of Dubai ruler's nephew missing, says lawyer
articles.sentiment_target: Sheikh Saeed bin Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum
articles.rephrased_article: A British human rights lawyer, David Haigh, says that Zeynab Javadli, the former wife of a nephew of the ruler of Dubai, has gone missing.  Javadli's home in Dubai is empty and locked, with her mother having reported finding it so after arriving from Azerbaijan where she is from. Her disappearance follows years of a bitter custody battle with her ex-husband, Sheikh Saeed bin Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum, and has sparked concerns about potential security threats.  Haigh, who has been advocating for Javadli, believes the situation resembles the case of Princess Latifa, another daughter of the ruler of Dubai, who attempted to escape captivity in 2018. He is calling on the international community to demand confirmation of her whereabouts and welfare.

articles.title: Kuki body opposes Manipur voter roll revision, flags exclusion of 59,000 displaced people | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Kuki Inpi Manipur has expressed opposition to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Manipur, citing concerns about displaced people's participation. The organization demands that "satisfactory arrangements" be made to ensure all displaced persons are included in the process. The Election Commission of India (ECI) is considering deploying special Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) for internally displaced persons in Manipur and plans to make arrangements for around 14,000-15,000 eligible individuals.

articles.title: Countries unrelated to conflicts also facing consequences: Mohan Bhagwat on Iran-US tensions | Mumbai News - The Indian Express

articles.title: Citi initiates coverage on 4 Indian power equipment stocks; sees up to 33% upside. Own any? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Citigroup initiated "Buy" calls on Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions. The report highlights the Indian transmission plan, which includes a significant investment in HVDC infrastructure, as a key driver for growth in the sector.  Citigroup believes that Hitachi Energy India is best positioned to capitalize on this opportunity due to its higher probability of near-term HVDC wins and strong growth prospects.

articles.title: Malviya Nagar fire: CM Rekha Gupta meet victims, announces compensation; LG hold high-level meet | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced an ex-gratia of Rs 10 lakh for the families of the victims and Rs 5 lakh for those injured in a fire at Flourish Stays, a bed-and-breakfast facility in South Delhi.  Gupta directed departments to conduct a thorough investigation, audit fire safety standards, and take strict action against negligence. The Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu chaired a meeting with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to discuss a comprehensive plan for stronger urban governance, improved infrastructure, and enhanced structural safety across Delhi.  The LG directed the MCD to implement a time-bound strategy to detect and demolish unauthorized constructions.

articles.title: Sherpa survives 6-day Everest ordeal, crawls down 12km from 25k feet sans food, oxygen - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 52-year-old Sherpa guide, Dawa ‘Hillary’ Sherpa, was found alive after six days lost on Mount Everest. He survived by scavenging for food and water near Base Camp despite enduring difficult weather conditions without supplies.  Chris Thrall, a British climber who was part of the group that included Dawa, has been criticized online for not returning to search for him, but later expressed relief at his survival. Dawa was rescued by a Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee (SPCC) cleanup team and is currently receiving treatment in Kathmandu.

articles.title: India not Vishwaguru yet, still inadequately prepared: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mohan Bhagwat, RSS chief, and Kumar Mangalam Birla, industrialist, addressed the economic challenges facing India during a recent event in Nagpur. They emphasized that while India's era has arrived, its preparedness to lead the world is still lacking.  They argued that building national capabilities is crucial for seizing emerging opportunities amid global instability caused by wars and market fluctuations, particularly with the advent of AI.

articles.title: Donald Trump: US lawmakers defy Trump in voting to end Iran war, plan to deny him funds for MAGA insurrectionists - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Republican lawmakers in the House of Representatives voted to prevent President Trump from continuing the war against Iran without congressional authorization, marking a rare instance of independent thought within the party. This action was supported by four Republicans and joined by Democrats.  The resolution faces an uphill battle in the Senate, where it would require a presidential veto override. Meanwhile, senators are expected to vote on amendments blocking the Trump administration's plan for a $1.8 billion fund to compensate individuals who claim they were wrongfully prosecuted or investigated by the Biden administration. Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina and Senator John Cornyn of Texas have led resistance against this proposal.  While Trump remains popular with Republican voters, these actions suggest a growing sense of congressional independence within the party.

articles.title: How Sir Alex Younger UK Spy Used Mother-In-Law's Blackberry Jam To Win Over Hamid Karzai
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Alex Younger, former head of Britain's foreign intelligence agency MI6, died at age 62 after leading the agency from 2014 to 2020. Younger oversaw key events like Brexit, the rise of the Islamic State group, and Russia tensions during his tenure. He was knighted in 2019 and worked as an adviser for Goldman Sachs until his death.

articles.title: The TikTok Ban Was Never About TikTok | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: A new documentary, "TikTok Never Dies," chronicles the legal battles surrounding a potential ban on TikTok in the United States. The film details the saga from President Donald Trump's initial threat to block the app in 2020 to the eventual sale of its US operations in 2026.  The documentary explores how TikTok became a symbol for broader American anxieties about social media, China, and political power.

articles.title: Tricked In Thailand, Rescued From Laos: Gujarat Sisters' Ordeal
articles.rephrased_article: Two sisters from Gujarat's Anand district have been rescued from a human trafficking syndicate in Laos after being missing for nearly 20 days. Mitesh Patel, the Member of Parliament from Anand, initiated high-level interventions with the Ministry of External Affairs and diplomatic channels to locate the women and ensure their safety. A joint operation involving the Indian Embassy, the Ministry of External Affairs, the Laos police, and the Laos army successfully located and secured the sisters in the Houaphanh province of Laos. The sisters are now under the care of local authorities in Laos and will be repatriated to India soon.

articles.title: Auburn University student goes missing in Japan during family vacation, had a fight with mom over use of ChatGPT - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Alabama family is searching for their 20-year-old son, Weston Higginbotham, who went missing in Kyoto, Japan on May 29th.  Weston, a student at Auburn University, was last seen around 8 p.m. walking alone in the city's Yamashina area before his phone location was lost. The family reported him missing to local authorities after he left Kyoto Station alone at 6 pm that day, and has circulated a missing person flyer in Japanese.  The FBI is now involved in the search alongside the Japanese police and civilian volunteers.

articles.title: Meta Silently Added Face-Recognition Code for Its Smart Glasses to Millions of Phones | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta has quietly embedded face-recognition technology into its AI app, called "NameTag," which identifies people captured by Meta's smart glasses and triggers notifications when a match is found.  The feature, initially discovered in January, was integrated into the companion app for Meta's smart glasses, including Ray-Ban and Oakley models. While Meta claims it will take a "thoughtful approach" before deploying face recognition technology, the company has already deployed core components of the system to users' phones. Privacy advocates warn that this move could normalize consumer-level face recognition, which they argue would give stalkers and abusers easy access to dangerous technology.

articles.title: Auburn University student goes missing in Japan during family vacation, had a fight with mom over use of ChatGPT - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Alabama family is searching for their 20-year-old son, Weston Higginbotham, who went missing in Kyoto, Japan, after leaving a train station on May 29th.  Weston, an experienced traveler and Auburn University student, was last seen around 8 p.m. walking alone in the city’s Yamashina area before his phone location was lost. The family reports that Weston's behavior is out of character, as he always shared his location with them. The Japanese police, civilian volunteers, and the FBI are involved in the search for him.

articles.title: 12 More Ministers To Be Part Of Himanta Sarma Cabinet, Oath Tomorrow
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Sarma, the Chief Minister of Assam, announced his 12-member cabinet for a swearing-in ceremony on Friday. The new council will have 17 ministers, with two vacancies to be filled over the year.  The newly appointed ministers include Ashwini Ray Sarkar, Ashok Singhal, Bimal Borah, Biswajit Daimary, Jayanta Mallabaruah, Kaushik Rai, Keshab Mahanta, Krishnendu Paul, Nilima Devi, Pijush Hazarika, Ranoj Pegu, and Susanta Borgohain.  The swearing-in ceremony will formally constitute the new council under Sarma's leadership.

articles.title: Archaeologists find ancient matrilineal society in Turkiye’s Catalhoyuk | History | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Turkiye have discovered evidence of a matrilineal society at the Neolithic settlement of Catalhoyuk, dating back 9,000 years.  The study of skeletons and grave goods suggests that women remained in their homes while men moved away, indicating a matrilocal system. This discovery challenges traditional understandings of early human societies, which were often patrilineal and patriarchal. The settlement's unique features include densely packed housing clusters, agricultural production, rituals, and ornamentation, suggesting an egalitarian society with no evidence of organized violence.  The findings have sparked debate about the origins of social structures and the potential role of a "mother goddess" in early human societies.

articles.title: Rights group sues South African government over US arms exports | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A South African human rights organization, Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC), has filed a lawsuit against the South African government seeking to suspend arms export permits to the United States.  SALC argues that these transfers may violate domestic law and international peace and security standards set by the National Conventional Arms Control Act. The case is significant as it challenges arms exports to a permanent member of the UN Security Council on human rights grounds, marking the first such challenge in South Africa.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Martin Luther King Jr.: “True peace is not merely the absence of tension; it is…” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Martin Luther King Jr.'s quote, "True peace is not merely the absence of tension; it is the presence of justice," challenges the common assumption that peace equates to a lack of conflict. He argued that appearances can be deceiving, as visible calm may mask underlying inequalities and injustices.  This distinction between surface-level peace and true justice remains relevant today, prompting individuals and societies to examine deeper issues rather than simply focusing on outward stability.

articles.rephrased_article: Citigroup initiated "Buy" calls on Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions, while maintaining a "Neutral" rating for Siemens Energy. Citigroup believes that this will create substantial opportunities for domestic T&D OEMs, particularly those specializing in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) technology.

articles.title: Looking Beyond Andhra Pradesh, Pawan Kalyan To NDTV On Party's Growth Plan
articles.rephrased_article: Pawan Kalyan, Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister, accused the Telangana Congress government of denying him a constitutional right to hold a meeting on Telangana Formation Day. He criticized the party's divisive politics and claimed that the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), which fought for Telangana's creation, never obstructed him during its 10-year rule.  Kalyan also expressed his belief that the NDA could have capitalized on opportunities like those presented by C Joseph Vijay's success in Tamil Nadu and urged former BJP leader K Annamalai to remain in politics. He praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his leadership and commitment to national integrity.

articles.title: Phoebe Bridgers Ditched the Internet to Hype Up Her New Music. It’s Working | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Phoebe Bridgers has been teasing a new album release with a series of surprise shows across the United States. The singer's team has implemented a no-phone policy at each venue, creating an intimate and mysterious experience for fans who have been actively investigating potential locations and themes through online speculation.  Fans have shared photos and theories about the tour, leading to a sense of community and anticipation around the upcoming album release. Tidal is sponsoring one of the shows at Madison Square Garden, where tickets are $1.

articles.title: Lt Governor Manoj Sinha On Kashmiri Pandit Exodus: 'Common Kashmiri Has Done No Wrong'
articles.rephrased_article: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha addressed an interfaith conference in Srinagar, asserting that the common people of Kashmir were not responsible for the events that transpired there. He stated that Kashmiris have a better understanding of India than other citizens and urged them to work within the framework of the Constitution.  Sinha also highlighted Jammu and Kashmir's high ranking in nationwide celebrations of 150 years of "Vande Mataram," emphasizing the region's harmonious environment. Senior RSS leader, Indresh Kumar, attended the conference.

articles.title: Ronaldo, Messi at World Cup: Who else is playing their final tournament? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Luka Modric, Neymar Jr., Manuel Neuer, Mohamed Salah, Kevin de Bruyne, Virgil van Dijk, Sadio Mane, and Guillermo Ochoa are among the players who could be playing their final World Cup tournament.  The 2026 World Cup in North America may mark the end of an era for many of these football legends, as they approach the twilight of their careers.

articles.title: Israel must allow ICRC to visit Palestinians in prison, Supreme Court rules | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s Supreme Court unanimously rejected a government policy banning representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) from visiting Palestinian detainees in Israeli prisons. The court ruled that the ban violated both Israeli and international law, and ordered its repeal.  The decision comes amid growing concerns about the treatment of Palestinian detainees in Israeli custody.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article reports a potential violation of human rights and international law.

articles.title: Trump official-turned-foe John Bolton accepts plea deal in documents case | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Former President Donald Trump national security advisor, John Bolton, is set to accept a plea deal in a case related to the handling of classified documents.  Bolton, now a prominent critic of the former president, will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security documents and pay a fine over $2 million. The Department of Justice indicted him in October for 18 counts related to his alleged mishandling and sharing of classified information. Bolton's case is part of a larger pattern of legal actions against Trump critics, including former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James.

articles.title: Video: Lufthansa Boeing 787's Nose Gear Collapses At Airport, Several Injured
articles.rephrased_article: A Lufthansa Boeing 787-9 suffered a nose gear collapse while parked at Frankfurt Airport on Thursday, injuring several staff members. The incident occurred while the aircraft was stationary at a gate and forced authorities to launch an investigation into the cause of the collapse.  The airline stated that no passengers were onboard at the time and has canceled flight LH450 from Frankfurt to Los Angeles. articles.title: Haryana's New EV Rule: Will Your Cab, E-Commerce Deliveries Cost More Now?
articles.rephrased_article: The Haryana government has implemented a new policy that prohibits the addition of new petrol and diesel vehicles to commercial fleets in its NCR districts. While this transition may initially increase cab fares due to higher upfront costs for operators, long-term benefits include lower operating expenses, improved vehicle maintenance, and potentially more reliable service. The policy aims to reduce urban emissions, improve air quality, and contribute to cleaner transportation across India. articles.title: Indonesia arrests officials in crackdown on corruption | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia’s deputy minister for immigration affairs, Silmy Karim, has been arrested following an investigation into alleged corruption in the administration of immigration documents. Budi Prasetyo, spokesperson for the anticorruption agency KPK, confirmed the arrest and stated that Karim was questioned for about 10 hours before being transferred to detention. The KPK has also identified seven other suspects in the case, which is believed to have occurred from 2023 to 2024 while Karim served as director general for immigration affairs under former President Joko Widodo.

articles.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to conditional ceasefire | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a conditional ceasefire after US-brokered talks in Washington, DC. The agreement requires Hezbollah to cease fire and remove operatives from southern Lebanon.  Despite the ceasefire announcement, Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel will continue military operations in Lebanon and maintain its presence in areas occupied since March.  Hezbollah also launched attacks on Israeli soldiers and targets, while Iran's foreign minister warned of a full-scale resumption of war if Beirut is attacked. The US President separately sought to separate talks on the conflict in Lebanon from those on the US-Israeli war on Iran.

articles.title: Brunson scores 30 as Knicks upset Spurs in NBA Finals opener | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-95 in game one of the NBA Finals, overcoming a 14-point third-quarter deficit.  Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 30 points, including eight straight points in the fourth quarter that sealed the victory. Victor Wembanyama had 26 points and 12 rebounds for the Spurs but shot poorly from the field. The series continues Friday night in San Antonio.

articles.title: 'Inflated Bills, Gold Mine': Rajesh Exports And A Rs 15 Lakh Crore Question
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) barred Rajesh Exports and its promoter-chairman, Rajesh Mehta, from accessing the securities market due to allegations of massive revenue misrepresentation spanning five financial years. The regulator alleges that nearly all of Rajesh Exports' reported revenues came from overseas subsidiaries, with a discrepancy of Rs 15.15 lakh crore in reported revenues compared to verified subsidiary records. SEBI also questioned investments in gold mining assets in Africa and transactions involving Affluence Shares Pvt. Ltd., raising concerns about the company's financial health and governance.  The investigation is ongoing, and Rajesh Exports denies all allegations, while investors have reacted with severe market punishment for the company.

articles.title: China bans four New Zealand lawmakers over visit to Taiwan | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China has banned four New Zealand lawmakers for visiting Taiwan in May, citing interference in its internal affairs and the sending of "wrong signals" to the ruling Democratic Progressive Party. The Chinese embassy stated that the visit violated China's opposition to visits by members of parliament to Taiwan, a self-governing democracy claimed by China as part of its territory.  The lawmakers have condemned the ban, calling it foreign interference and maintaining their right to engage with Taiwan.

articles.rephrased_article: The FIFA World Cup 2026 kicks off on June 11th in Mexico City with a match between Mexico and South Africa. NASA officials confirmed that while MAVEN's failure will cause a slight delay in relaying Mars science data from rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance, the agency's other spacecraft are still operational. The mission provided valuable insights into atmospheric loss on Mars, including its interaction with solar storms and the discovery of auroras.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay Allocates Lone Rajya Sabha Seat To Congress
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Vijay of Tamil Nadu has allotted the vacant Rajya Sabha seat to the Congress, a move seen as strengthening the alliance between the two parties. articles.title: UP Man Kills Family Over Property, Gets Killed By Friend Who Helped In Crime
articles.rephrased_article: Police in South Malaka, India, are investigating the deaths of three family members. articles.title: Exclusive | Licence in accountant’s name: How South Delhi hotel owner bypassed rules | Delhi News - The Indian Express

articles.rephrased_article: Israel carried out air strikes on Gaza City overnight, killing at least nine people, including four children. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that talks with the United States have not progressed despite open communication channels.
